title: Core Banking Ledger Replication Lag — Balance Inconsistency During Peak Hours

content.summary: Replication lag on the PostgreSQL read-replica cluster reached 45 minutes during the lunch-hour peak on 2024-02-20, causing mobile banking and ATM balance queries to return stale balances. Approximately 78,000 customers saw incorrect available balance figures.

timeline.event: Replication lag monitoring alert fires at 5-minute lag threshold
Lag reaches 15 minutes; mobile-banking-api begins serving stale balances
Lag peaks at 45 minutes; 78,000 active sessions affected
DBA team identifies long-running analytics query blocking vacuum on primary
Analytics query terminated; replication begins catching up
Replication lag returns to < 30 s; incident resolved

content.root_cause: A newly deployed data-warehouse ETL job executed a 3-hour full-table scan on the core banking ledger's primary PostgreSQL instance without a statement_timeout. The scan prevented autovacuum from completing on the transactions table, causing WAL bloat that overwhelmed replication throughput to read replicas.
contributing_factors: ETL job deployed to production without statement_timeout configuration
Analytics workloads not segregated from OLTP primary — no read-replica routing for analytics
Replication lag alerting threshold was 5 minutes (should have been 2 minutes for balance-sensitive paths)
Mobile-banking-api had no circuit breaker to fall back to primary reads on stale-data detection

immediate: Force manual vacuum on transactions table
Switch mobile-banking-api balance endpoint to read from primary temporarily
short_term: Add statement_timeout = 300 s to all ETL database roles (JIRA DB-441)
Route analytics ETL to a dedicated analytics replica (JIRA DB-442)
Lower replication lag alert threshold to 2 minutes (JIRA OPS-2215)
long_term: Implement read-your-writes consistency for mobile balance API
Introduce dedicated analytics PostgreSQL instance separate from OLTP cluster
Automated ETL query plan analysis before production deployment
